claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a child - his name is Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have Alex who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask: Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex.

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I give money towards his upkeep each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you're contributing financially.

To determine your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about Alex's living situation. Who does Alex currently live with?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more important question about your financial contributions:

How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week, and what does this cover (for example, food, clothes, pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £10 a week - it helps with things like clothes and bits and pieces he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to check one more important detail about your contributions.

The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child. For you to qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you would normally need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards Alex's upkeep.

You mentioned you contribute £10 per week. Is this your total contribution, or do you also make other contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as additional payments, buying things directly for him, or other forms of support)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's my total contribution - just the £10 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (such as his mum)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum already claims Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

1. **Only one person can claim**: Alex's mother is already claiming Child Benefit for him, and only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.

2. **Insufficient contributions**: Since Alex doesn't live with you, you would need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards his upkeep to qualify. The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child, but you're contributing £10 per week, which falls short of this requirement.

If you wanted to claim Child Benefit for Alex in the future, you would need to:
- Have his mother agree to stop claiming (and she would need to contact the Child Benefit Office)
- Either have Alex come to live with you, OR increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week towards his upkeep
- Make a new claim yourself

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
